readings.text: 10 Finally, be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power. 11 Put on the full armor of God, so that you can take your stand against the devil’s schemes. 12 For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this dark world and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms. 13 Therefore put on the full armor of God, so that when the day of evil comes, you may be able to stand your ground, and after you have done everything, to stand.

14 Stand firm then, with the belt of truth buckled around your waist, with the breastplate of righteousness in place, 15 and with your feet fitted with the readiness that comes from the gospel of peace. 16 In addition to all this, take up the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one. 17 Take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.
18 And pray in the Spirit on all occasions with all kinds of prayers and requests. With this in mind, be alert and always keep on praying for all the Lord’s people.

story: Last week we learned that the Holy Spirit grows love, joy, peace, and more good fruit in us. Today Paul tells the church to be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power. Put on the full armor of God, so that you can take your stand against the devil’s schemes. We say this simply, with care. We do not act out a fight, and we do not make a scary game of the devil. God gives us his armor so we can stand strong in him.

For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this dark world and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms. We tell that simply. This is not a fight against people. Therefore put on the full armor of God, so that when the day of evil comes, you may be able to stand your ground, and after you have done everything, to stand.

Stand firm then, with the belt of truth buckled around your waist, with the breastplate of righteousness in place, and with your feet fitted with the readiness that comes from the gospel of peace. In addition to all this, take up the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one. We say the arrows simply. We do not act out fire or shooting. Take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God. The sword is God’s word, not a toy for hitting people. And pray in the Spirit on all occasions with all kinds of prayers and requests. With this in mind, be alert and always keep on praying for all the Lord’s people.
Next week we will hear that Jesus teaches us how to pray to our Father in heaven.
weeks.enochLine: God gives us his armor so we can stand strong in him!
enochActivities: Activity: Stand strong. Plant your feet and say: God gives me his armor so I can stand!
Activity: Belt of truth. Pretend to buckle a belt and say: Truth! God helps me stand!
elijahQuestions: In Ephesians 6:10–11, where does Paul say we should be strong, and why should we put on the full armor of God?
In Ephesians 6:12–13, is our struggle against flesh and blood, and what does the armor help us do?
In Ephesians 6:14–17, can you name the pieces of God’s armor, and what is the sword of the Spirit?
In Ephesians 6:18, what does Paul tell us to do, and for whom should we keep on praying?
elijahAnswers: Be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power. Put on the full armor of God, so that you can take your stand against the devil’s schemes (Ephesians 6:10–11).

No. Our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the powers of this dark world and the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms. We say that simply. The armor helps us stand our ground, and after we have done everything, to stand (Ephesians 6:12–13).

The belt of truth, the breastplate of righteousness, feet fitted with the readiness that comes from the gospel of peace, the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God (Ephesians 6:14–17).
Pray in the Spirit on all occasions with all kinds of prayers and requests. Be alert and always keep on praying for all the Lord’s people (Ephesians 6:18).
jordynQuestions: Paul says, Be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power, and then, Put on the full armor of God (Ephesians 6:10–11). What is the difference between trying to be strong on your own and standing in armor God gives?
Our struggle is not against flesh and blood (Ephesians 6:12). How should that change the way you treat people when a day feels hard?
The armor ends with the word of God and with prayer (Ephesians 6:17–18). Next week Jesus will teach us how to pray to our Father in heaven. How do God’s armor and prayer belong together?
jordynAnswers: The strength is the Lord’s, and the armor is his gift. We do not invent a tough face and call it faith. We put on what God gives—truth, righteousness, peace, faith, salvation, and his word—so we can stand in him.
People are not the enemy. We do not use hard words or pretend fights against flesh and blood. We stand in God’s armor, and we treat people as people, even when the day is dark.

The sword of the Spirit is the word of God, and then Paul says to pray in the Spirit on all occasions. Armor is not only something we put on and forget. We stand, and we keep praying. Next week Jesus will teach us the words to pray to our Father.
weeks.jordynApplication: God gives us his armor so we can stand strong in him (Ephesians 6:10–18). This week, choose one piece of the armor—truth, righteousness, the gospel of peace, faith, salvation, or the word of God—and practice it in a real moment at home. Then pray for someone in the Lord’s people. Next week we will hear that Jesus teaches us how to pray to our Father in heaven.
weeks.applicationCheck: Ask her later in the week which piece of God’s armor she practiced, or whether she prayed for someone. If it is fitting, thank God together that he gives us his armor so we can stand, and that we can pray for all the Lord’s people.
weeks.prayer: Father, thank you that we can be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power. Thank you for the full armor of God: truth, righteousness, the gospel of peace, faith, salvation, and the word of God. Help us stand firm in you, and teach us to pray in the Spirit on all occasions for all the Lord’s people. In Jesus’ name, Amen.

dailies.label: Day 2 · Passage
dailies.focus: Be strong in the Lord, and put on the full armor of God so you can stand.
dailies.verse: Finally, be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power. Put on the full armor of God, so that you can take your stand against the devil’s schemes.
dailies.enoch: Plant your feet and say: Be strong in the Lord! God gives me his armor!
dailies.elijah: In Ephesians 6:10–11, where should we be strong, and what should we put on?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power. Put on the full armor of God, so that you can take your stand against the devil’s schemes.
dailies.jordyn: In Ephesians 6:12–13, why is it important that our struggle is not against flesh and blood, and what does the armor help us do when the day of evil comes?
dailies.jordynAnswer: This is not a fight against people. We say the hard words about dark powers simply, and we do not make a scary game of them. The armor helps us stand our ground, and after we have done everything, to stand.
dailies.action: Read Ephesians 6:10–13 out loud. Then thank God that we can be strong in the Lord, and that he gives us his armor so we can stand.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that we can be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power. Thank you for the full armor of God, so we can stand. Help us remember this is not a fight against people. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Paul says, Finally, be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power. Put on the full armor of God, so that you can take your stand against the devil’s schemes. Our struggle is not against flesh and blood. Therefore put on the full armor of God, so that when the day of evil comes, you may be able to stand your ground, and after you have done everything, to stand. We tell this simply. We do not act out a fight, and we do not make a scary game of the devil.
dailies.enochActivity: Plant your feet, stand tall, and say: I can stand, because God is strong!
dailies.elijah2: In Ephesians 6:13, what two times does Paul use the word stand?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Stand your ground, and after you have done everything, to stand.
dailies.jordyn2: Why does Paul keep saying stand, instead of telling us to go start a fight (Ephesians 6:11–13)?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The armor is given so we can take our stand and hold our ground in the Lord. The strength is his. We are not told to attack people.
dailies.passageText: 10 Finally, be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power. 11 Put on the full armor of God, so that you can take your stand against the devil’s schemes. 12 For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this dark world and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms. 13 Therefore put on the full armor of God, so that when the day of evil comes, you may be able to stand your ground, and after you have done everything, to stand.

dailies.label: Day 3 · Game
dailies.focus: We name the pieces of God’s armor, because he gives them so we can stand.
dailies.verse: Stand firm then, with the belt of truth buckled around your waist, with the breastplate of righteousness in place,
dailies.enoch: Pretend to buckle a belt and say: Belt of truth!
dailies.elijah: In Ephesians 6:14–15, which three pieces does Paul name first?
dailies.elijahAnswer: The belt of truth, the breastplate of righteousness, and feet fitted with the readiness that comes from the gospel of peace.
dailies.jordyn: Truth, righteousness, and the gospel of peace are not toys (Ephesians 6:14–15). What might it look like to stand in these at home, without acting out a battle?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Tell the truth. Do what is right. Be ready to live the good news of peace with the people in your house. The armor is for standing in the Lord, not for pretending to hit someone.
dailies.action: Play Put on the armor. Take turns naming a piece and making a simple, calm gesture: buckle truth, place a hand on your chest for righteousness, take a ready step for the gospel of peace. Do not swing, shout, or act out a fight.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you for the belt of truth, the breastplate of righteousness, and feet fitted with the readiness that comes from the gospel of peace. Help us stand in these gifts at home. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Stand firm then, with the belt of truth buckled around your waist, with the breastplate of righteousness in place, and with your feet fitted with the readiness that comes from the gospel of peace. Today we name these gifts and remember they come from God. We do not turn them into a fight game.
dailies.enochActivity: Take one ready step and say: Gospel of peace! God helps me stand!
dailies.elijah2: In Ephesians 6:15, what are our feet fitted with?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: The readiness that comes from the gospel of peace.
dailies.jordyn2: Why might peace belong in a picture of armor (Ephesians 6:15)?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: God’s armor is not for starting fights with people. The good news of peace makes us ready to stand, and to walk in peace.
dailies.passageText: 14 Stand firm then, with the belt of truth buckled around your waist, with the breastplate of righteousness in place, 15 and with your feet fitted with the readiness that comes from the gospel of peace.

dailies.label: Day 4 · Passage
dailies.focus: Take up the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.
dailies.verse: Take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.
dailies.enoch: Place a hand on your head and say: Helmet of salvation! Then hold your hands like an open Bible and say: The word of God!
dailies.elijah: In Ephesians 6:16–17, what three gifts does Paul name, and what is the sword of the Spirit?
dailies.elijahAnswer: The shield of faith, the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.
dailies.jordyn: The shield of faith can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one (Ephesians 6:16). How should we talk about that line with care, and what does faith do?
dailies.jordynAnswer: We say the arrows simply. We do not act out fire or shooting. Faith is a gift from God that helps us stand when a hard thought or a hard day comes. We trust the Lord, and we are not left uncovered.
dailies.action: Read Ephesians 6:14–17 out loud. Then thank God for faith, salvation, and his word, and remember the sword is the word of God, not a toy for hitting.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you for the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God. Help us stand in these gifts, and love your word. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: In addition to all this, take up the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one. We say that simply, and we do not act it out. Take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God. The sword is Scripture, not a stick for pretend fighting.
dailies.enochActivity: Hold your hands like an open book and say: The sword of the Spirit is the word of God!
dailies.elijah2: In Ephesians 6:16, what does the shield of faith do?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: With it you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one.
dailies.jordyn2: Why is it good that the sword of the Spirit is named as the word of God (Ephesians 6:17)?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: God does not send us out to invent our own weapon. He gives us his word. We stand by what he has said.
dailies.passageText: 16 In addition to all this, take up the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one. 17 Take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.

dailies.label: Day 5 · Challenge
dailies.focus: Stand firm in the armor God gives, and remember this is not a fight against people.
dailies.verse: Therefore put on the full armor of God, so that when the day of evil comes, you may be able to stand your ground, and after you have done everything, to stand.
dailies.enoch: Plant your feet and say: After I have done everything, I can stand—in the Lord!
dailies.elijah: In Ephesians 6:13–14, what does Paul tell us to do, and what is the first piece he names when we stand firm?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Put on the full armor of God so you may be able to stand your ground, and after you have done everything, to stand. Stand firm then, with the belt of truth buckled around your waist.
dailies.jordyn: A challenge to stand can feel like a dare to be tough (Ephesians 6:13). How is this challenge different?
dailies.jordynAnswer: The armor is God’s, and the strength is the Lord’s. The challenge is to put on what he gives and to stand, not to pick a fight or pretend we are strong alone.
dailies.action: Today’s challenge: Stand firm in one real way—tell the truth, or take a peaceful step toward someone at home. Then thank God that he gives the armor. Do not act out a battle.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that when we put on the full armor of God, we can stand our ground, and after we have done everything, stand. Help us stand in truth and peace today. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Therefore put on the full armor of God, so that when the day of evil comes, you may be able to stand your ground, and after you have done everything, to stand. Stand firm then, with the belt of truth buckled around your waist. Today’s challenge is to stand in a real, quiet way at home, not to play at fighting.
dailies.enochActivity: Buckle an imaginary belt and plant your feet: Truth! I can stand in the Lord!
dailies.elijah2: In Ephesians 6:14, what is buckled around your waist when you stand firm?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: The belt of truth.
dailies.jordyn2: What would it look like to stand your ground in truth without tearing another person down (Ephesians 6:12–14)?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Our struggle is not against flesh and blood. Standing in truth means telling the truth and staying with the Lord, not using words as weapons against people.
dailies.passageText: 13 Therefore put on the full armor of God, so that when the day of evil comes, you may be able to stand your ground, and after you have done everything, to stand. 14 Stand firm then, with the belt of truth buckled around your waist, with the breastplate of righteousness in place,

dailies.label: Day 6 · Prayer
dailies.focus: Pray in the Spirit on all occasions, and keep on praying for all the Lord’s people.
dailies.verse: And pray in the Spirit on all occasions with all kinds of prayers and requests. With this in mind, be alert and always keep on praying for all the Lord’s people.
dailies.enoch: Fold your hands and say: I can pray for the Lord’s people!
dailies.elijah: In Ephesians 6:18, when should we pray, and for whom should we keep on praying?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Pray in the Spirit on all occasions with all kinds of prayers and requests. Always keep on praying for all the Lord’s people.
dailies.jordyn: The armor comes first, and then prayer (Ephesians 6:17–18). Why might Paul want us to pray after we have just heard about standing in God’s armor?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Armor is not a costume we put on and then forget God. We stand in him, and we keep talking to him. Prayer is part of how we stay alert, and how we care for all the Lord’s people.
dailies.action: Pray today’s prayer out loud as a family. Then each person can pray a short request for someone who belongs to the Lord.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that we can pray in the Spirit on all occasions with all kinds of prayers and requests. Make us alert, and help us keep on praying for all the Lord’s people. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: And pray in the Spirit on all occasions with all kinds of prayers and requests. With this in mind, be alert and always keep on praying for all the Lord’s people. After the armor, Paul turns us to prayer. Today we pray, and we remember the Lord’s people.
dailies.enochActivity: Fold your hands, then open them like a thank-you, and say: Thank you, God! I can pray to you!
dailies.elijah2: In Ephesians 6:18, what two words describe how we should keep praying?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Always, and for all the Lord’s people. Paul says, always keep on praying for all the Lord’s people.
dailies.jordyn2: How can all kinds of prayers and requests keep prayer from feeling like only one stiff sentence (Ephesians 6:18)?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: We can thank, ask, and pray for others, on many kinds of days. Prayer belongs in ordinary life, not only in one special moment.
dailies.passageText: 18 And pray in the Spirit on all occasions with all kinds of prayers and requests. With this in mind, be alert and always keep on praying for all the Lord’s people.

dailies.label: Day 7 · Recap
dailies.focus: God gives us his armor so we can stand strong in him, and next Jesus will teach us how to pray.
dailies.verse: Finally, be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power.
dailies.enoch: Help a grown-up look toward the next room and say: Next week Jesus teaches us how to pray!
dailies.elijah: What is this week’s big idea, and can you name the pieces of God’s armor?
dailies.elijahAnswer: God gives us his armor so we can stand strong in him. The pieces are the belt of truth, the breastplate of righteousness, feet fitted with the gospel of peace, the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God. And we pray in the Spirit for all the Lord’s people.
dailies.jordyn: This week ends with prayer in the Spirit, and next week Jesus teaches us how to pray to our Father in heaven (Ephesians 6:18). What stays the same in both weeks?
dailies.jordynAnswer: God does not leave us to stand alone, and he does not leave us to invent prayer alone. He gives armor, and Jesus will teach us the words to pray to our Father. We stay with him.
dailies.action: Tell someone the week’s big idea: God gives us his armor so we can stand strong in him. Then thank God, and look ahead to the Lord’s Prayer.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that we can be strong in the Lord, and that you give us your full armor so we can stand. Thank you that we can pray in the Spirit for all the Lord’s people. Get our hearts ready to hear how Jesus teaches us to pray to our Father in heaven. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: This week we learned that God gives us his armor so we can stand strong in him. Be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power. Put on the full armor of God: truth, righteousness, the gospel of peace, faith, salvation, and the word of God. And pray in the Spirit on all occasions for all the Lord’s people. Next week Jesus will teach us how to pray to our Father in heaven.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up look toward the next room and say: Next week, the Lord’s Prayer!
dailies.elijah2: In Ephesians 6:17–18, what two gifts come at the end of the armor list?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: The sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God, and prayer in the Spirit on all occasions.
dailies.jordyn2: What stays the same when the story moves from God’s armor this week to the Lord’s Prayer next week?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The Lord who gives us armor so we can stand is the same Lord who teaches us to pray. We are not left to be strong, or to pray, on our own.
dailies.passageText: 10 Finally, be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power. 14 Stand firm then, with the belt of truth buckled around your waist, with the breastplate of righteousness in place, 15 and with your feet fitted with the readiness that comes from the gospel of peace. 16 In addition to all this, take up the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one. 17 Take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God. 18 And pray in the Spirit on all occasions with all kinds of prayers and requests. With this in mind, be alert and always keep on praying for all the Lord’s people.

weeks.title: The Lord's Prayer
weeks.selectLabel: Week 41 · The Lord's Prayer
weeks.nextUp: Week 42 · One body, many parts
weeks.bigIdea: Jesus teaches us how to pray to our Father in heaven.
weeks.scheduleNote: This is the Week 41 family lesson. The short daily bites are Days 2–7.

howSteps.title: Read together
howSteps.detail: Open the Read tab and read Matthew 6:9–10 out loud, then Matthew 6:11–13, then the whole prayer in Matthew 6:9–13.

howSteps.title: Talk it through
howSteps.detail: Still on Read, walk through the kid-language explanation so everyone gets the picture.

howSteps.title: Age parts
howSteps.detail: Use Enoch, Elijah, and Jordyn tabs. Keep the Parent key open for yourself.

howSteps.title: Pray
howSteps.detail: Close with the short family prayer on the Prayer tab, and pray the Lord’s Prayer together.

readings.text: 9 “This, then, is how you should pray: “‘Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, 10 your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.
11 Give us today our daily bread. 12 And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. 13 And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.’

9 “This, then, is how you should pray: “‘Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, 10 your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. 11 Give us today our daily bread. 12 And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. 13 And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.’

story: Last week we learned that God gives us his armor so we can stand strong in him, and that we can pray in the Spirit on all occasions. Today Jesus teaches us how to pray to our Father in heaven. This, then, is how you should pray. We say the prayer slowly. It is not a race, and it is not a magic chant. These are words Jesus gives us to pray.

Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Hallowed means God’s name is holy. We honor him. We ask for his kingdom and his will, not only our own plans. We call him our Father, not only my Father, because we belong to him together.

Give us today our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. Daily bread is the ordinary help we need today. Debts here are the wrongs we have done, and the wrongs others have done to us. We ask God to forgive us, and we also forgive. We ask him to keep us from temptation, and to deliver us from the evil one. We say that simply. We do not make a scary game of it. God can keep us and help us.
Next week we will hear that in Christ we are one body, and every person matters.
weeks.enochLine: Jesus teaches us how to pray to our Father in heaven!
enochActivities: Activity: Look up and say: Our Father in heaven!
Activity: Open your hands and say: Give us today our daily bread!
elijahQuestions: In Matthew 6:9, what does Jesus say this is, and how does the prayer begin?
In Matthew 6:9–10, what do we ask about God’s name, his kingdom, and his will?
In Matthew 6:11–12, what two things do we ask God to give us, and what have we also done?
In Matthew 6:13, what do we ask God not to lead us into, and what do we ask him to deliver us from?
elijahAnswers: This, then, is how you should pray. The prayer begins, Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name (Matthew 6:9).
Hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven (Matthew 6:9–10).
Give us today our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors (Matthew 6:11–12).
Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one (Matthew 6:13).
jordynQuestions: Jesus says, This, then, is how you should pray: Our Father in heaven (Matthew 6:9). What is the difference between rushing through these words and letting Jesus teach you how to pray?

The prayer asks, forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors (Matthew 6:12). How should that shape the way you treat someone at home after a wrong, without turning forgiveness into a game?
We pray to our Father, and next week we will hear that in Christ we are one body, and every person matters. How do those two truths belong together?
jordynAnswers: Jesus is teaching us how to pray, not giving us a chant to get through quickly. We come to our Father in heaven, we honor his holy name, and we ask for his kingdom and his will. The words are a gift to use slowly, with our hearts in them.

Debts here are real wrongs, not points to keep. We ask God to forgive us, and we also forgive. That is honest and kind. It is not pretending nothing happened, and it is not a race to say the words first.

We do not pray only as separate people. We say our Father, our daily bread, forgive us. Next week we will hear that in Christ we are one body, and every person matters. The same Father holds us together.
weeks.jordynApplication: Jesus teaches us how to pray to our Father in heaven (Matthew 6:9–13). This week, pray the Lord’s Prayer slowly once a day—out loud if you can. Pick one line to live: honor God’s holy name, ask for daily bread, forgive someone, or ask God to keep you from temptation. Next week we will hear that in Christ we are one body, and every person matters.
weeks.applicationCheck: Ask her later in the week whether she prayed the Lord’s Prayer slowly, or which line she tried to live. If it is fitting, pray Our Father in heaven together, and thank God that Jesus teaches us how to pray.
weeks.prayer: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us today our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. Thank you that Jesus teaches us how to pray to you. In Jesus’ name, Amen.

dailies.label: Day 2 · Passage
dailies.focus: Jesus teaches us to pray to our Father in heaven, and to honor his holy name.
dailies.verse: This, then, is how you should pray: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.
dailies.enoch: Look up and say: Our Father in heaven! Your name is holy!
dailies.elijah: In Matthew 6:9, how does Jesus say we should begin to pray, and what do we ask about God’s name?
dailies.elijahAnswer: This, then, is how you should pray: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name.
dailies.jordyn: In Matthew 6:9–10, why does it matter that we pray for God’s kingdom and his will, not only for our own plans?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Jesus teaches us to ask, your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. We honor our Father first. We want what he wants, here, as it is in heaven.
dailies.action: Read Matthew 6:9–10 out loud, slowly. Then thank God that Jesus teaches us how to pray to our Father in heaven.
dailies.prayer: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Thank you that we can pray to you. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Jesus says, This, then, is how you should pray: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Hallowed means God’s name is holy. We honor him. These words are a gift, not a race and not a magic chant.
dailies.enochActivity: Look up, then fold your hands, and say: Our Father! Your will be done!
dailies.elijah2: In Matthew 6:10, where do we ask for God’s will to be done?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: On earth as it is in heaven.
dailies.jordyn2: Jesus has us say our Father, not only my Father (Matthew 6:9). What does that tell you about prayer?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: We come to God together. He is the Father of his people, not a private helper for one child only.
dailies.passageText: 9 “This, then, is how you should pray: “‘Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, 10 your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.

dailies.label: Day 3 · Game
dailies.focus: We learn the words Jesus gives us, slowly, because he teaches us how to pray.
dailies.verse: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name,
dailies.enoch: Take turns saying: Our Father in heaven!
dailies.elijah: In Matthew 6:9–10, can you say the first part of the prayer Jesus gives?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.
dailies.jordyn: If this game is only about remembering lines, what would be missing from what Jesus is teaching (Matthew 6:9)?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Jesus is teaching us how to pray to our Father, not how to win a memory race. The words matter, and so does a heart that honors God’s holy name.
dailies.action: Play Pray like this. Take turns saying one short line of Matthew 6:9–10, calmly, with a simple gesture: look up for our Father in heaven, a hand on your heart for his holy name, open hands for his will. Do not race, shout, or turn the prayer into a joke.
dailies.prayer: Our Father in heaven, thank you for your holy name. Let your kingdom come, and your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: This, then, is how you should pray: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Today we practice the words slowly, so they can become a prayer, not a performance.
dailies.enochActivity: Look up and whisper: Hallowed be your name!
dailies.elijah2: In Matthew 6:9, what two words come right after Our Father?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: In heaven.
dailies.jordyn2: Why might Jesus want us to begin with our Father in heaven, before we ask for anything else (Matthew 6:9–10)?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Prayer starts with who God is. He is our Father in heaven, and his name is holy. Then we ask for his kingdom and his will.
dailies.passageText: 9 “This, then, is how you should pray: “‘Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, 10 your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.

dailies.label: Day 4 · Passage
dailies.focus: We ask for daily bread, and we ask to be forgiven as we also forgive.
dailies.verse: Give us today our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.
dailies.enoch: Open your hands and say: Give us today our daily bread!
dailies.elijah: In Matthew 6:11–12, what do we ask God to give us today, and what do we ask him to forgive?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Give us today our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.
dailies.jordyn: Debts in Matthew 6:12 are the wrongs we have done, and the wrongs others have done to us. How can you ask for forgiveness, and also forgive, without making it a score to keep?
dailies.jordynAnswer: We tell the truth: we need to be forgiven, and we also forgive. It is not pretending nothing happened, and it is not a game of who owes more. We bring both to our Father.
dailies.action: Read Matthew 6:11–13 out loud. Then thank God for daily bread, and if it is fitting, forgive someone at home, or ask to be forgiven.
dailies.prayer: Our Father, give us today our daily bread. Forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Give us today our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. Daily bread is the ordinary help we need today. Debts are real wrongs, taught simply. We do not make a scary game of the evil one. We ask our Father to keep us and to help us.
dailies.enochActivity: Open your hands, then gently fold them, and say: Forgive us, and help us forgive!
dailies.elijah2: In Matthew 6:13, what two things do we ask about temptation and the evil one?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.
dailies.jordyn2: Why might Jesus put daily bread and forgiveness next to each other in the same prayer (Matthew 6:11–12)?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: We need ordinary help for today, and we also need to be made right with God and with one another. Our Father cares for both.
dailies.passageText: 11 Give us today our daily bread. 12 And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. 13 And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.’

dailies.label: Day 5 · Challenge
dailies.focus: Pray one line of the Lord’s Prayer for real, and live it in an ordinary moment.
dailies.verse: Give us today our daily bread.
dailies.enoch: Open your hands and say: Give us today our daily bread! Thank you, Father!
dailies.elijah: In Matthew 6:11–12, what do we ask God to give us today, and what have we also done when we ask him to forgive us?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Give us today our daily bread. We ask him to forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.
dailies.jordyn: A challenge to pray can turn into a performance (Matthew 6:9–12). How is today’s challenge different from showing off a prayer?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Jesus is teaching us how to pray to our Father, not how to look holy. The challenge is to use one real line—daily bread, or forgiveness—with your heart in it, in an ordinary moment at home.
dailies.action: Today’s challenge: Choose one line from Matthew 6:11–13 and live it—thank God for something you needed today, forgive someone, or ask him to keep you from temptation. Pray it simply, not as a show.

readings.text: 12 Just as a body, though one, has many parts, but all its many parts form one body, so it is with Christ. 13 For we were all baptized by one Spirit so as to form one body—whether Jews or Gentiles, slave or free—and we were all given the one Spirit to drink. 14 Even so the body is not made up of one part but of many. 15 Now if the foot should say, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,” it would not for that reason stop being part of the body. 16 And if the ear should say, “Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body,” it would not for that reason stop being part of the body. 17 If the whole body were an eye, where would the sense of hearing be? If the whole body were an ear, where would the sense of smell be? 18 But in fact God has placed the parts in the body, every one of them, just as he wanted them to be. 19 If they were all one part, where would the body be? 20 As it is, there are many parts, but one body.

21 The eye cannot say to the hand, “I don’t need you!” And the head cannot say to the feet, “I don’t need you!” 22 On the contrary, those parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable, 23 and the parts that we think are less honorable we treat with special honor. And the parts that are unpresentable are treated with special modesty, 24 while our presentable parts need no special treatment. But God has put the body together, giving greater honor to the parts that lacked it, 25 so that there should be no division in the body, but that its parts should have equal concern for each other. 26 If one part suffers, every part suffers with it; if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it. 27 Now you are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it.

story: Last week Jesus taught us how to pray to our Father in heaven, and we said our Father, not only my Father. Today Paul shows us why that word our matters. Just as a body, though one, has many parts, but all its many parts form one body, so it is with Christ. For we were all baptized by one Spirit so as to form one body—whether Jews or Gentiles, slave or free—and we were all given the one Spirit to drink. Even so the body is not made up of one part but of many. In Christ we are one body, and every person matters.

Now if the foot should say, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,” it would not for that reason stop being part of the body. And if the ear should say, “Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body,” it would not for that reason stop being part of the body. We do not make a joke of a foot or an ear, and we do not tease anyone about their body. The point is belonging. You still belong, even if you feel different. But in fact God has placed the parts in the body, every one of them, just as he wanted them to be. As it is, there are many parts, but one body.

The eye cannot say to the hand, “I don’t need you!” And the head cannot say to the feet, “I don’t need you!” On the contrary, those parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable, and the parts that we think are less honorable we treat with special honor. And the parts that are unpresentable are treated with special modesty. We say that simply, with care. We do not laugh at anyone’s body. God has put the body together so that there should be no division, but that its parts should have equal concern for each other. If one part suffers, every part suffers with it; if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it. Now you are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it.
Next week we will hear that God promised Abraham a family, and God kept his word.

elijahQuestions: In 1 Corinthians 12:12–14, what is the church like, and is the body made up of only one part?
In 1 Corinthians 12:15–18, if the foot says, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,” does it stop being part of the body, and who has placed the parts in the body?
In 1 Corinthians 12:21–23, what can the eye not say to the hand, and how should we treat parts that seem weaker or less honorable?
In 1 Corinthians 12:26–27, what happens when one part suffers or is honored, and what does Paul say we are?
elijahAnswers: Just as a body, though one, has many parts, but all its many parts form one body, so it is with Christ. The body is not made up of one part but of many (1 Corinthians 12:12–14).
No. It would not for that reason stop being part of the body. God has placed the parts in the body, every one of them, just as he wanted them to be (1 Corinthians 12:15–18).

The eye cannot say to the hand, “I don’t need you!” Those parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable, and the parts that we think are less honorable we treat with special honor (1 Corinthians 12:21–23).
If one part suffers, every part suffers with it; if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it. Now you are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it (1 Corinthians 12:26–27).
jordynQuestions: Paul says we were all baptized by one Spirit so as to form one body—whether Jews or Gentiles, slave or free (1 Corinthians 12:13). What does that tell you about who belongs in Christ’s body?

The eye cannot say to the hand, “I don’t need you!” (1 Corinthians 12:21), and the parts that seem weaker are indispensable (1 Corinthians 12:22). How should that change the way you treat someone who seems quieter, younger, or less noticed?
We have learned that we are one body in Christ, and next week we will hear that God promised Abraham a family, and God kept his word. How do those two truths belong together?
jordynAnswers: Belonging in the body is not for one kind of person only. The one Spirit has made one body of many kinds of people. If you are in Christ, you belong, and so do people who are not just like you.

You may not say you do not need them. The parts that seem weaker are indispensable, and we treat with special honor the ones we might be tempted to overlook. Every person matters, and we have equal concern for each other.

The body of Christ is a people God has made his own. Next week we will hear that God promised Abraham a family, and God kept his word. The same God who keeps his promises is the God who places each part in the body, just as he wanted them to be.
weeks.jordynApplication: In Christ we are one body, and every person matters (1 Corinthians 12:12–27). This week, notice someone who might feel left out—at home, at church, or among friends—and treat them with equal concern. Do not say, even quietly, “I don’t need you!” Next week we will hear that God promised Abraham a family, and God kept his word.
weeks.applicationCheck: Ask her later in the week whom she noticed, or how she showed equal concern. If it is fitting, thank God together that in Christ we are one body, and that every person matters.
weeks.prayer: Father, thank you that just as a body has many parts, so it is with Christ. Thank you that we were all given the one Spirit, and that you have placed every part in the body just as you wanted them to be. Teach us not to say, “I don’t need you!” Help us treat one another with honor, suffer with those who suffer, and rejoice with those who are honored. In Christ we are one body, and every person matters. In Jesus’ name, Amen.

dailies.elijah: In 1 Corinthians 12:26–27, what do we do when one part suffers or is honored, and what are we in Christ?
dailies.elijahAnswer: If one part suffers, every part suffers with it; if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it. Now you are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it.
dailies.jordyn: Prayer for the body can stay general (1 Corinthians 12:25–27). What is one real person you can name before God today, with equal concern?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Equal concern means we bring real people to our Father: someone who is suffering, or someone who has been honored. We ask God to help us suffer with them, or rejoice with them, as parts of one body.
dailies.action: Pray today’s prayer out loud as a family. Then each person can name one person in the body of Christ and ask God to help you care for them.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that if one part suffers, every part suffers with it, and if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it. We are the body of Christ, and each one of us is a part of it. Give us equal concern for each other. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: There should be no division in the body, but its parts should have equal concern for each other. If one part suffers, every part suffers with it; if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it. Today we pray as people who belong to one body, and we ask our Father to make that concern real.
dailies.enochActivity: Fold your hands, then open them toward the family, and say: Thank you, God! We belong together!
dailies.elijah2: In 1 Corinthians 12:25, what does God not want in the body, and what does he want its parts to have?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: There should be no division in the body, but its parts should have equal concern for each other.
dailies.jordyn2: How can prayer help a body that is tempted to say, “I don’t need you!” (1 Corinthians 12:21, 25)?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: We ask our Father to change that sentence. We thank him for the parts we might overlook, and we ask for equal concern, because he has put the body together.
dailies.passageText: 25 so that there should be no division in the body, but that its parts should have equal concern for each other. 26 If one part suffers, every part suffers with it; if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it. 27 Now you are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it.

dailies.label: Day 7 · Recap
dailies.focus: In Christ we are one body, and next we will hear that God promised Abraham a family.
dailies.verse: Just as a body, though one, has many parts, but all its many parts form one body, so it is with Christ.
dailies.enoch: Help a grown-up look toward the next room and say: Next week, God kept his promise to Abraham!
dailies.elijah: What is this week’s big idea, and can you say what happens if a foot feels it does not belong, or if an eye says, “I don’t need you!”?
dailies.elijahAnswer: In Christ we are one body, and every person matters. If the foot says, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,” it would not for that reason stop being part of the body. The eye cannot say to the hand, “I don’t need you!” God has placed every part just as he wanted them to be.
dailies.jordyn: We have learned that we are the body of Christ, and next week we will hear that God promised Abraham a family, and God kept his word (1 Corinthians 12:27). What stays the same in both weeks?
dailies.jordynAnswer: God makes a people and keeps them. We are one body in Christ, and each one of us is a part of it. Next week we will hear that God promised Abraham a family, and God kept his word. The same God places the parts and keeps his promises.
dailies.action: Tell someone the week’s big idea: In Christ we are one body, and every person matters. Then look ahead to Abraham, and the God who keeps his word.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that in Christ we are one body, and every person matters. Thank you that you have placed each part just as you wanted. Get our hearts ready to hear that you promised Abraham a family, and you kept your word. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: This week we learned that in Christ we are one body, and every person matters. Just as a body has many parts, so it is with Christ. God has placed every part just as he wanted them to be. The eye cannot say, “I don’t need you!” If one part suffers, every part suffers with it. Now you are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it. Next week we will hear that God promised Abraham a family, and God kept his word.
dailies.enochActivity: Help a grown-up look toward the next room and say: Next week, Abraham: God keeps his promise!
dailies.elijah2: In 1 Corinthians 12:27, what does Paul say we are, and what is each one of us?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Now you are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it.
dailies.jordyn2: What stays the same when the story moves from one body, many parts this week to Abraham’s promised family next week?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The God who places every part in the body is the God who promised Abraham a family and kept his word. We belong to a people he has made, and he does not forget his promises.
dailies.passageText: 12 Just as a body, though one, has many parts, but all its many parts form one body, so it is with Christ. 15 Now if the foot should say, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,” it would not for that reason stop being part of the body. 18 But in fact God has placed the parts in the body, every one of them, just as he wanted them to be. 21 The eye cannot say to the hand, “I don’t need you!” And the head cannot say to the feet, “I don’t need you!” 26 If one part suffers, every part suffers with it; if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it. 27 Now you are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it.

readings.text: 1 The LORD had said to Abram, “Go from your country, your people and your father’s household to the land I will show you. 2 “I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you; I will make your name great, and you will be a blessing. 3 I will bless those who bless you, and whoever curses you I will curse; and all peoples on earth will be blessed through you.” 4 So Abram went, as the LORD had told him; and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he set out from Harran. 5 He took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, all the possessions they had accumulated and the people they had acquired in Harran, and they set out for the land of Canaan, and they arrived there. 6 Abram traveled through the land as far as the site of the great tree of Moreh at Shechem. At that time the Canaanites were in the land. 7 The LORD appeared to Abram and said, “To your offspring I will give this land.” So he built an altar there to the LORD, who had appeared to him. 8 From there he went on toward the hills east of Bethel and pitched his tent, with Bethel on the west and Ai on the east. There he built an altar to the LORD and called on the name of the LORD. 9 Then Abram set out and continued toward the Negev.

1 After this, the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision: “Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your very great reward.” 2 But Abram said, “Sovereign LORD, what can you give me since I remain childless and the one who will inherit my estate is Eliezer of Damascus?” 3 And Abram said, “You have given me no children; so a servant in my household will be my heir.” 4 Then the word of the LORD came to him: “This man will not be your heir, but a son who is your own flesh and blood will be your heir.” 5 He took him outside and said, “Look up at the sky and count the stars—if indeed you can count them.” Then he said to him, “So shall your offspring be.” 6 Abram believed the LORD, and he credited it to him as righteousness.

1 Now the LORD was gracious to Sarah as he had said, and the LORD did for Sarah what he had promised. 2 Sarah became pregnant and bore a son to Abraham in his old age, at the very time God had promised him. 3 Abraham gave the name Isaac to the son Sarah bore him. 4 When his son Isaac was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him, as God commanded him. 5 Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him. 6 Sarah said, “God has brought me laughter, and everyone who hears about this will laugh with me.” 7 And she added, “Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne him a son in his old age.”

story: Last week we learned that in Christ we are one body, and every person matters. Today we hear how God promised Abram a family, and how God kept his word. The same man is later called Abraham when the promised son is born. The LORD had said to Abram, Go from your country, your people and your father’s household to the land I will show you. I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you; I will make your name great, and you will be a blessing. I will bless those who bless you, and whoever curses you I will curse; and all peoples on earth will be blessed through you. So Abram went, as the LORD had told him. He was seventy-five years old. The LORD appeared to Abram and said, “To your offspring I will give this land.” So he built an altar there to the LORD, who had appeared to him.

Later the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision: “Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your very great reward.” Abram still had no child, and he wondered about the promise. We say that simply. It is not a joke. Then the word of the LORD came to him: “This man will not be your heir, but a son who is your own flesh and blood will be your heir.” He took him outside and said, “Look up at the sky and count the stars—if indeed you can count them.” Then he said to him, “So shall your offspring be.” Abram believed the LORD, and he credited it to him as righteousness.

Years went by, and they waited. We do not leave today’s readings to tell other parts of the story. We wait with them for the word God had already spoken. Now the LORD was gracious to Sarah as he had said, and the LORD did for Sarah what he had promised. Sarah became pregnant and bore a son to Abraham in his old age, at the very time God had promised him. Abraham gave the name Isaac to the son Sarah bore him. When his son Isaac was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him, as God commanded him. We say that simply, as Abraham’s obedience. Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him. Sarah said, “God has brought me laughter, and everyone who hears about this will laugh with me.” And she added, “Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne him a son in his old age.” We laugh with her for joy, not at her. God promised Abraham a family, and God kept his word.
Next week we will hear that God was with Joseph, and he used even hard things for good.
weeks.enochLine: God promised Abraham a family, and God kept his word!
enochActivities: Activity: Look up and say: God keeps his promises, like stars in the sky!
Activity: Take one step and say: Abram went, as the LORD told him!
elijahQuestions: In Genesis 12:1–4, what did the LORD tell Abram to do, and did Abram go?
In Genesis 12:7, what did the LORD promise to give Abram’s offspring, and what did Abram do?
In Genesis 15:4–6, who would be Abram’s heir, what did the LORD say about the stars, and what did Abram do?
In Genesis 21:1–7, what did the LORD do for Sarah, what did they name the son, and what did Sarah say about laughter?
elijahAnswers: The LORD told him to go from his country, his people, and his father’s household to the land the LORD would show him, and that he would make him into a great nation and bless him. So Abram went, as the LORD had told him (Genesis 12:1–4).
The LORD said, “To your offspring I will give this land.” So Abram built an altar there to the LORD, who had appeared to him (Genesis 12:7).

A son who is your own flesh and blood will be your heir. The LORD said, “Look up at the sky and count the stars—if indeed you can count them.” Then he said, “So shall your offspring be.” Abram believed the LORD, and he credited it to him as righteousness (Genesis 15:4–6).

The LORD was gracious to Sarah as he had said, and did for Sarah what he had promised. They named the son Isaac. Sarah said, “God has brought me laughter, and everyone who hears about this will laugh with me.” (Genesis 21:1–6).
jordynQuestions: The LORD promised to make Abram into a great nation, and to bless all peoples on earth through him (Genesis 12:2–3), and Abram went, as the LORD had told him (Genesis 12:4). What is the difference between hearing a promise and actually going?

Abram still had no child when the LORD said, “So shall your offspring be.” Abram believed the LORD, and he credited it to him as righteousness (Genesis 15:5–6). What does it mean to believe God when you cannot yet see the promise?
God kept his word at the very time he had promised, and next week we will hear that God was with Joseph, and he used even hard things for good. What stays the same about God in both stories?
jordynAnswers: Abram did not only hear the blessing. He left his country and his father’s household, and he went, as the LORD had told him. Faith takes the next step God has given, even before the great nation can be seen.
Believing is trusting the LORD’s word, not waiting until you can already count the family. Abram had no child yet, and he still believed. The LORD credited it to him as righteousness.

God keeps his word. He was gracious to Sarah as he had said, at the very time he had promised. Next week we will hear that God was with Joseph, even in hard things, and used them for good. The same God is faithful.
weeks.jordynApplication: God promised Abraham a family, and God kept his word (Genesis 12:1–9; 15:1–6; 21:1–7). This week, thank God for one promise he has already kept, and take one ordinary step of trust, the way Abram went as the LORD had told him. Next week we will hear that God was with Joseph, and he used even hard things for good.
weeks.applicationCheck: Ask her later in the week which promise she thanked God for, or what step of trust she took. If it is fitting, thank God together that he promised Abraham a family, and that he kept his word.
weeks.prayer: Father, thank you that you told Abram to go, and that he went as you had told him. Thank you that you said, “To your offspring I will give this land.” Thank you that you said, “So shall your offspring be.” Thank you that Abram believed you, and that you were gracious to Sarah as you had said, and did what you had promised. You promised Abraham a family, and you kept your word. Help us trust you. In Jesus’ name, Amen.

dailies.jordyn: In Genesis 12:4–7, what did Abram do, and what did the LORD say about the land?
dailies.jordynAnswer: So Abram went, as the LORD had told him. The LORD appeared to Abram and said, “To your offspring I will give this land.” So he built an altar there to the LORD, who had appeared to him.
dailies.action: Read Genesis 12:1–9 out loud. Then thank God that Abram went as the LORD had told him, and that God promised him a family and a land.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that you called Abram to go, and that he went as you had told him. Thank you that you said, “To your offspring I will give this land.” Help us trust your word. In Jesus’ name, Amen.

dailies.enochActivity: Take one step, then fold your hands, and say: Thank you, God! Abram went!
dailies.elijah2: In Genesis 12:2, what did the LORD say he would make Abram into?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you; I will make your name great, and you will be a blessing.
dailies.jordyn2: Why might it matter that all peoples on earth will be blessed through Abram (Genesis 12:3), not only Abram’s own house?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: God’s promise is bigger than one family album. He would bless Abram, and through him bless all peoples on earth.

dailies.label: Day 3 · Game
dailies.focus: We remember the promise, and we practice going as the LORD told Abram.
dailies.verse: The LORD appeared to Abram and said, “To your offspring I will give this land.”
dailies.enoch: Point ahead and say: To your offspring I will give this land!
dailies.elijah: In Genesis 12:1 and 12:4, what did the LORD tell Abram to do, and what did Abram do?
dailies.elijahAnswer: The LORD told him to go from his country, his people, and his father’s household to the land the LORD would show him. So Abram went, as the LORD had told him.
dailies.jordyn: This game is about trusting and going, not about pretending to be old (Genesis 12:4). What should we remember if we talk about Abram being seventy-five?
dailies.jordynAnswer: We say his age simply, because the story does. We do not make a joke of it. The point is that Abram went, as the LORD had told him, and God had promised a family and a land.
dailies.action: Play Go as the LORD told him. Take turns taking a calm step across the room, then stopping to build a tiny altar with two hands, and saying, “To your offspring I will give this land.” Do not race, and do not make a joke of Abram’s age.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that Abram went as you had told him, and that you promised, “To your offspring I will give this land.” Help us trust you and take the next step you give. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Go from your country, your people and your father’s household to the land I will show you. So Abram went, as the LORD had told him. The LORD appeared to Abram and said, “To your offspring I will give this land.” So he built an altar there. Today we practice going and remembering the promise, with care.
dailies.enochActivity: Take one step and say: I will go, because God keeps his word!
dailies.elijah2: In Genesis 12:8, after the LORD appeared, what else did Abram do?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: He pitched his tent, built an altar to the LORD, and called on the name of the LORD.
dailies.jordyn2: What is the difference between building an altar and just walking past the promise (Genesis 12:7–8)?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: Abram stopped to worship. He called on the name of the LORD in the land God had promised. The promise was not only a trip. It was a life with God.

dailies.label: Day 4 · Passage
dailies.focus: The LORD promised Abram a son, and Abram believed the LORD.
dailies.verse: Abram believed the LORD, and he credited it to him as righteousness.
dailies.enoch: Look up and say: Abram believed the LORD!
dailies.elijah: In Genesis 15:1 and 15:4–5, what did the LORD say to Abram, and what did he promise about a son and the stars?
dailies.elijahAnswer: “Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your very great reward.” “This man will not be your heir, but a son who is your own flesh and blood will be your heir.” He said, “Look up at the sky and count the stars—if indeed you can count them.” Then he said, “So shall your offspring be.”
dailies.jordyn: In Genesis 15:2–6, Abram still had no child, and he believed the LORD. How should we talk about that waiting, and what did God credit to him?
dailies.jordynAnswer: We say it simply. Abram wondered about the promise because he had no child yet. That is not a joke. Abram believed the LORD, and he credited it to him as righteousness.
dailies.action: Read Genesis 15:1–6 out loud. Then look up, if you can see the sky, and thank God that Abram believed the LORD, and that God keeps his promises.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that you said, “Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your very great reward.” Thank you that you promised, “So shall your offspring be.” Thank you that Abram believed you. Help us believe you too. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: The word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision: “Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your very great reward.” Abram still had no child. The LORD said, “This man will not be your heir, but a son who is your own flesh and blood will be your heir.” He said, “Look up at the sky and count the stars—if indeed you can count them.” Then he said, “So shall your offspring be.” Abram believed the LORD, and he credited it to him as righteousness.
dailies.enochActivity: Look up and say: Look at the stars! God keeps his promises!
dailies.elijah2: In Genesis 15:5, after the LORD told Abram to count the stars, what did he say?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: “So shall your offspring be.”
dailies.jordyn2: Why is it important that Abram believed the LORD before the son was born (Genesis 15:6)?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: He trusted God’s word when he could not yet see the child. The LORD credited that belief to him as righteousness.
dailies.passageText: 1 After this, the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision: “Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your very great reward.” 2 But Abram said, “Sovereign LORD, what can you give me since I remain childless and the one who will inherit my estate is Eliezer of Damascus?” 3 And Abram said, “You have given me no children; so a servant in my household will be my heir.” 4 Then the word of the LORD came to him: “This man will not be your heir, but a son who is your own flesh and blood will be your heir.” 5 He took him outside and said, “Look up at the sky and count the stars—if indeed you can count them.” Then he said to him, “So shall your offspring be.” 6 Abram believed the LORD, and he credited it to him as righteousness.

dailies.label: Day 5 · Challenge
dailies.focus: Trust God’s word, as Abram believed the LORD, even before he could see the promise.
dailies.verse: He took him outside and said, “Look up at the sky and count the stars—if indeed you can count them.” Then he said to him, “So shall your offspring be.”
dailies.enoch: Look up and say: So shall your offspring be! I can trust God!
dailies.elijah: In Genesis 15:5–6, what did the LORD tell Abram to look at, what did he promise, and what did Abram do?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Look up at the sky and count the stars—if indeed you can count them. “So shall your offspring be.” Abram believed the LORD, and he credited it to him as righteousness.
dailies.jordyn: A challenge to believe can turn into a show of big words (Genesis 15:6). How is today’s challenge different?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Abram believed the LORD. The challenge is to trust God’s word in an ordinary way today, not to sound brave. God is the one who keeps the promise.
dailies.action: Today’s challenge: Name one way you will trust God’s word today—a kind step, a honest prayer, or a thank-you for a promise he has already kept. Do it simply, not as a show.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that Abram believed you, and that you credited it to him as righteousness. Help us trust your word today, even when we cannot yet see the end. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: “Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your very great reward.” “Look up at the sky and count the stars—if indeed you can count them.” “So shall your offspring be.” Abram believed the LORD, and he credited it to him as righteousness. Today’s challenge is to trust that same faithful God in an ordinary moment.
dailies.enochActivity: Look up, then fold your hands, and say: I believe you, God!
dailies.elijah2: In Genesis 15:1, what two things did the LORD say he is for Abram?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: I am your shield, your very great reward.
dailies.jordyn2: How can the LORD’s word, Do not be afraid, Abram, help a person who is still waiting on a promise (Genesis 15:1, 6)?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The LORD himself is the shield and the reward. Abram believed him before the child was born. We can take the next trusting step without seeing everything yet.
dailies.passageText: 1 After this, the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision: “Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your very great reward.” 5 He took him outside and said, “Look up at the sky and count the stars—if indeed you can count them.” Then he said to him, “So shall your offspring be.” 6 Abram believed the LORD, and he credited it to him as righteousness.

dailies.label: Day 6 · Prayer
dailies.focus: We thank God that he was gracious to Sarah, and that he kept his promise.
dailies.verse: Now the LORD was gracious to Sarah as he had said, and the LORD did for Sarah what he had promised.
dailies.enoch: Clap once, gently, and say: God kept his promise!
dailies.elijah: In Genesis 21:1–5, what did the LORD do for Sarah, what did they name the son, and how old was Abraham?
dailies.elijahAnswer: The LORD was gracious to Sarah as he had said, and did for Sarah what he had promised. They named the son Isaac. Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.
dailies.jordyn: In Genesis 21:6–7, Sarah talks about laughter and about nursing a child in old age. How should we hear her words?
dailies.jordynAnswer: Sarah said, “God has brought me laughter, and everyone who hears about this will laugh with me.” And she added, “Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne him a son in his old age.” We laugh with her for joy, because God kept his word. We do not make a joke of her age or her body.
dailies.action: Pray today’s prayer out loud as a family. Thank God that he did what he had promised, and that Isaac was born at the very time God had promised.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that you were gracious to Sarah as you had said, and that you did what you had promised. Thank you for Isaac, and for Sarah’s joy: “God has brought me laughter, and everyone who hears about this will laugh with me.” You promised Abraham a family, and you kept your word. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
dailies.teach: Now the LORD was gracious to Sarah as he had said, and the LORD did for Sarah what he had promised. Sarah bore a son to Abraham in his old age, at the very time God had promised him. They named him Isaac. When his son Isaac was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him, as God commanded him. We say that simply, as obedience. Sarah said, “God has brought me laughter, and everyone who hears about this will laugh with me.” God kept his word. Today we pray with thanks.
dailies.enochActivity: Open your hands and say: Thank you, God! You kept your promise!
dailies.elijah2: In Genesis 21:2, when was Isaac born?
dailies.elijahAnswer2: Sarah became pregnant and bore a son to Abraham in his old age, at the very time God had promised him.
dailies.jordyn2: Why does it matter that this happened at the very time God had promised (Genesis 21:1–2)?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: God’s word is not late and not empty. He was gracious as he had said, and he did what he had promised.
dailies.passageText: 1 Now the LORD was gracious to Sarah as he had said, and the LORD did for Sarah what he had promised. 2 Sarah became pregnant and bore a son to Abraham in his old age, at the very time God had promised him. 3 Abraham gave the name Isaac to the son Sarah bore him. 4 When his son Isaac was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him, as God commanded him. 5 Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him. 6 Sarah said, “God has brought me laughter, and everyone who hears about this will laugh with me.” 7 And she added, “Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne him a son in his old age.”

dailies.label: Day 7 · Recap
dailies.focus: God promised Abraham a family, and he kept his word. Next, God was with Joseph in hard things.
dailies.verse: Abram believed the LORD, and he credited it to him as righteousness.
dailies.enoch: Help a grown-up look toward the next room and say: Next week, God was with Joseph!
dailies.elijah: What is this week’s big idea, and can you tell how God kept his promise, from the call of Abram to the birth of Isaac?
dailies.elijahAnswer: God promised Abraham a family, and God kept his word. The LORD told Abram to go, and promised to make him a great nation. Abram believed the LORD when he still had no child, and the LORD said, “So shall your offspring be.” Then the LORD was gracious to Sarah as he had said, and Isaac was born at the very time God had promised.
dailies.jordyn: We have seen that God kept his promise to Abraham, and next week we will hear that God was with Joseph, and he used even hard things for good. What stays the same about God?
dailies.jordynAnswer: God is faithful. He keeps his word, and he does not leave his people. Next week we will hear that God was with Joseph even in hard things, and used them for good. The same God who kept his promise to Abraham was with Joseph too.
dailies.action: Tell someone the week’s big idea: God promised Abraham a family, and God kept his word. Then look ahead to Joseph, and the God who can use even hard things for good.
dailies.prayer: Father, thank you that you promised Abraham a family, and that you kept your word. Thank you that Abram believed you, and that Isaac was born at the very time you had promised. Get our hearts ready to hear that you were with Joseph, and that you used even hard things for good. In Jesus’ name, Amen.

The LORD said, “To your offspring I will give this land.” He also said, “So shall your offspring be.” Abram believed the LORD. Then the LORD was gracious to Sarah as he had said, and Isaac was born. Next week we will hear that God was with Joseph, and he used even hard things for good.

dailies.jordyn2: What stays the same when the story moves from Abraham’s kept promise this week to Joseph’s hard road next week?
dailies.jordynAnswer2: The same God keeps his word and stays with his people. He promised Abraham a family and kept his word. Next week we will hear that he was with Joseph, and used even hard things for good.
